transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-29
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Rahul (Zenith Head of ML), Sophie (Zenith Infra), Tomás (Zenith CTO)
---
Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
Zenith is evaluating exit from a mixed stack (OpenAI hosted + self-hosted vLLM/TGI) toward either Redwood Hosted for speed of migration or Redwood Dedicated/Private for data residency and cost predictability. Main concerns: compatibility of vLLM/TGI prompts and model variants, eval parity (quality + latency), VPC/KMS for private deployment, and pricing comparison. Next steps: trial eval, SOC2 + VPC docs, architecture deep dive.
Topics: migration path, eval parity, performance benchmarks, security (SOC2/SSO/KMS), deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private), timeline for pilot.
Action items (also below): see action_items metadata
---
Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. I'm Maya from Redwood, this is Liam, our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:10] Tomás (CTO): Hey, good — running a bit tight today, but ready.
[00:13] Rahul (Head of ML): Morning, thanks. We'll try to keep this focused. We sent a short doc earlier about our current stack.
[00:20] Maya: Yep saw that, thanks. Quick round — Rahul, can you summarize the current setup and what's driving the migration?
[00:28] Rahul: Sure. So we've been running a hybrid setup. Production chat features hit OpenAI for a subset of traffic for safety/latency. For lower cost and custom models we use a self-hosted stack: vLLM + TGI on GPU infra. It works but ops is rough — memory/kv cache tuning, kernel mismatches, and we see a lot of tail latency spikes. Also infra costs are creeping.
[00:48] Sophie (Infra): And we have compliance needs for EU data residency, plus some customers require dedicated instances, so that's another driver.
[00:55] Liam (SE): Got it. So two parallel asks: 1) faster time-to-value and a cleaner hosted experience to reduce ops, and 2) an option for dedicated/private with VPC and KMS for sensitive customers. That maps to Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated/Private.
[01:10] Tomás: Right. And we need confidence that our prompt behavior and eval metrics remain par with what we have on vLLM/TGI. We can't get worse results for certain financial summarization flows.
[01:20] Maya: Totally. We do a lot of model onboarding tests, and Liam will run parity checks. Quick question — are you tightly coupled to a specific model family today or is the stack model-agnostic?
[01:31] Rahul: We're mostly running TGI backed LLaMA derivatives for cost reasons, with some experiments on Claude and GPT-4 via OpenAI for higher-quality routes. So mixed.
[01:40] Liam: That helps. For parity we typically test the canonical prompt sets plus your regression prompts. We'll run Redwood-hosted and if you want, a Dedicated private pilot — same runtime semantics, different placement. Note that some vLLM behaviors like certain kv-cache warmup patterns can differ; we try to surface those.
[01:55] Sophie: A couple of questions on security — do you support SSO for the console, RBAC, audit logs? And for private deployments, KMS integrations?
[02:04] Maya: Yes to SSO and RBAC on the Console, audit logs are built-in. Private has integrations with customer KMS/HSMs and can run in customer VPCs. We can share SOC2 redacted. I'll attach the docs.
[02:16] Tomás: Good. Cost — can you give a ballpark for token pricing v. our self-hosted spend? We're trying to justify the move to execs.
[02:24] Maya: We'll share pricing bands. Typically Hosted is higher per-token than optimized Dedicated or Private but you trade off ops. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching to reduce unit cost. We'll put together a spreadsheet comparing your current cost per 1M tokens vs hosted/dedicated projections.
[02:39] Rahul: On evals — our biggest worry is hallucination on the finance summarizer. Small changes to tokenizer/decoding across runtimes can change outputs. How deterministic is Redwood's runtime relative to vLLM/TGI?
[02:50] Liam: Good call-out. Determinism depends on the model variant and sampling settings. We keep consistent top-k/top-p and seed behaviors, but lower-level kernel ordering can cause minor diffs. We focus on regressions vs your golden set — if there's a drop we diagnose whether it's model-fp differences, tokenizer mapping, or runtime decoding. For critical flows we can run A/B with automatic fallbacks to your previous provider during pilot.
[03:12] Sophie: Do you support bringing our own model artifacts? We have tuned weights and a quantized repo already.
[03:18] Liam: Yes, BYO model artifacts is possible in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we have curated model catalog; we can onboard models you provide but there are vetting steps. Quantization formats sometimes require conversion; we have tooling for common formats (ggml, q4/q8, awq) but there can be friction depending on the build.
[03:33] Tomás: If we need on-prem because of data regulations, what's the timeline and footprint?
[03:38] Maya: On-prem deployments vary — typical pilot for Private starts with a small cluster (2-4 nodes) and we iterate. Delivery time depends on procurement and networking but we've done pilots in 4-8 weeks historically. For VPC private control plane it's faster. We'll scope with your infra team.
[03:52] Rahul: Latency targets: our p50 target is 120ms for short chat turns, p95 under 500ms for most flows. Does Redwood support GPU placement that can hit those with similar models?
[04:04] Liam: Yes, with appropriate GPU types and batching configs we can hit those numbers on Dedicated. For Hosted we have regional endpoints and optimized kernels; we can run a bench that replicates your prompt distribution to validate.
[04:16] Sophie: On network egress for EU data — if we use Hosted, can we restrict data to EU regions only?
[04:22] Maya: Hosted supports region pins for inference. For stricter controls we recommend Dedicated/Private.
[04:28] Rahul: What's the recommended migration sequencing? Start with non-prod via Hosted, then Dedicated?
[04:32] Liam: Many customers start with Hosted for a quick parity check and to avoid infra provisioning, then move to Dedicated when they need reserved capacity or Private for data residency. But if you have firm compliance constraints, starting with Private can make sense.
[04:47] Tomás: We also run a lot of long-context summarization (8k+). How does Redwood handle KV cache and memory pressure? vLLM gave us fine-grained control.
[04:55] Liam: Our runtime provides KV cache management and we surface cache hits and evictions in the Console. There are quantization and compilation knobs we can tune; we'll capture your sequence length distribution in the benchmark so we recommend GPU and batching settings.
[05:08] Rahul: Any limitations on model size or custom layers? We sometimes use adapters and small LoRA-style tweaks.
[05:14] Liam: Adapters/LoRA are supported but onboarding works slightly differently across Hosted vs Private. For Hosted we might host a variant if it passes vetting; for Private you can deploy your exact artifacts. We can document the exact onboarding path for your artifacts.
[05:28] Maya: Quick check — timeline and success criteria? Rahul, what do you need to see to recommend Redwood internally?
[05:34] Rahul: We want parity on quality for the top 3 flows, latency at or below p95 500ms for those flows, and a cost projection showing TCO improvements or clear ops savings within 6 months. Also security docs for exec review.
[05:46] Maya: Great — that's actionable. We'll run the parity eval and share the pricing + SOC2 artifacts.
[05:50] Tomás: What about falling back to OpenAI if there's a regression during pilot? We don't want outages.
[05:56] Liam: We can configure fallbacks at the routing layer to route to your existing provider if Redwood serving fails or quality drops on canary. That reduces risk during pilot.
[06:06] Sophie: Link sharing — can we get the benchmark template and a short onboarding checklist?
[06:11] Maya: Yes will send. We'll include a small Prompts + Eval kit. Also note we have a shared drive with an example benchmark: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/zenith-sample and I'll attach the spreadsheet.
[06:25] RahuI (sic): (laughter) Rahul: that's rahul with an L, but yes thanks.
[06:30] Liam: (laugh) got it. So next steps we'll run a 1k prompt evaluation against your three canonical flows on Redwood-hosted, capture p50/p95 and cost, and then if you want we'll spin a Dedicated pilot.
[06:45] Tomás: Do you require an NDA for the pilot? We might need one for certain customer prompt examples.
[06:50] Maya: We can operate under your existing NDA or sign ours, whichever's faster. We'll make sure any sensitive prompts are redacted in shared artifacts.
[06:58] Rahul: A couple of technical nitpicks — tokenization differences: can you map our tokenizer steps? Our current pipeline pre-tokenizes and occasionally uses custom tokenization for domain terms.
[07:08] Liam: We can ingest pre-tokenized sequences for Dedicated/private; for Hosted we can accept raw text and we'll document tokenizer mapping. If you have custom tokens we may need a small conversion step. We'll include that in the onboarding checklist.
[07:20] Sophie: For Dedicated pricing, do you offer committed capacity with autoscaling? Our traffic is spiky end of month.
[07:27] Maya: Yes committed pools with configurable autoscaling policy and burst capacity. We can size based on your traffic curve.
[07:33] Rahul: Any existing customers in fintech vertical with similar constraints?
[07:37] Maya: We have a couple of finance customers — we can share redacted case studies. I'll include a short reference list.
[07:44] Tomás: On the technical deep dive, we'd like Liam to join and perhaps one of your runtime engineers. Will that be possible?
[07:49] Liam: Absolutely. We can schedule a 60–90 minute session to walk through model onboarding, tokenizer mapping, and KV cache tuning.
[07:57] Maya: Ok, let's lock dates after the trial results. Anything else urgent?
[08:01] Rahul: No, just want concrete numbers.
[08:04] Maya: Understood. We'll aim to send the initial artifacts by tomorrow and the eval results in about a week.
[08:10] Tomás: Sounds good.
[08:13] (crosstalk)
[08:15] Maya: Quick recap — Liam runs parity eval (1k prompts) on Redwood Hosted, attaches latency/cost spreadsheet; Maya sends SOC2/VPC/KMS docs + pricing bands + benchmark template; Rahul shares canonical prompt set and current cost metrics; schedule deep-dive next week.
[08:33] Sophie: Perfect. Thank you.
[08:36] Maya: Thanks all — we'll follow up with links.
[08:40] (meeting ends)
